[attribute-publication-format]
=== `@publication-format` Format of Publication

Format or medium of the document (for example, “`print`”). This element has several uses: to describe the format/medium of a standards document for a publication date or other lifecycle date (<<element-release-date,`<release-date>`>>) or for an organization-specific lifecycle date (<<element-meta-date,`<meta-date>`>>); to name the format/medium of a document being cited as part of a bibliographic reference; or to name the format/medium for an ISBN or similar identifier.

#### OPTIONAL on many elements; click for list and usage

<<element-date,`<date>`>>, <<element-element-citation,`<element-citation>`>>, <<element-isbn,`<isbn>`>>, <<element-issn,`<issn>`>>, <<element-meta-date,`<meta-date>`>>, <<element-mixed-citation,`<mixed-citation>`>>, <<element-nlm-citation,`<nlm-citation>`>>, <<element-pub-date,`<pub-date>`>>, <<element-release-date,`<release-date>`>>
|===
| Value| Meaning

| Text, numbers, or special characters| The format for the publication of this standards document, for example, “`print`”, “`online`”, “`epub`”. This value is not constrained, so any standards organization is free to use the
                        values it needs for processing.
| Restriction| This is an optional attribute; there is no default.
|===
